title: Approve the art style guide
question:
The art style guide draft is ready: measured palette ramps, outline and shape rules, contrast standards, reserved overlay colors (like the magenta that only ever means pest scent), an animation budget, and what all this implies for the eventual full reskin. Everything generated since has followed it informally; your sign-off makes it the law.

At the look session, also settle how the picture of a character or animal ends: must its edge be a hard cut between fully drawn and absent pixels, or may the edge use partly transparent pixels? The guide does not say. The fourth look promises softer edges, so that look depends on your answer. The hand-edits section of the art direction guide records the evidence behind this question.

Also settle where a character or animal ends and the ground begins. On 2026-09-16 you erased 84 pixels from the neighbour, the chicken and the crow, all at the bottom of each figure and almost all of them the generator's cream backdrop; the guide has no rule for that spot. The art director recommends nothing under the feet: a figure's lowest drawn pixel is where it stands, and if figures need shadows the game draws them. The alternatives, a shadow drawn into each character's picture or no rule at all, are in the guide beside the evidence.
why_now: The full reskin off placeholder art can't be scheduled until the style is locked — and every sprite generated before lock risks regeneration after it.

options.label: Approve as drafted
options.detail: The style guide becomes binding; the reskin can be planned.

options.label: Approve with amendments
options.detail: Write the changes in the judgment box.

options.label: Not yet — I want a look session
options.detail: A side-by-side render session against the current build first.

Same frame, seed and camera; derived by tools/derive_soft_edge_sprite.py with no image generation. On a sprite this small, the half-transparent ring makes thin parts such as legs and sleeves look see-through rather than softer.
